days.title: À et DE — comprendre les familles simplement
days.focus: Use the À family first (cities, countries, destinations, people, time), then the DE family (origin, belonging, topic), then food quantities; choose expressions by meaning in natural speech.

days.explanation:
DAY 29 — SIMPLE STUDENT NOTES
GOAL: Master À-family first (cities, countries, destinations, people, time), then DE-family (origin, belonging, topic); distinguish contractions from partitives and build real sentences.
ESTIMATED TIME: 55–65 minutes; study À, pause, then DE (two short sessions if needed)

0. ACTIVE RECALL FIRST (6–8 MIN)
Review due: Day 15, 22, 26, 28. Answer WITHOUT notes, say it aloud, then check. Add 2 old nouns with articles. Repeat any missed item tomorrow.

PART A — À FAMILY (LEARN THIS FIRST)
Start with ONE idea: À often points TO, AT or TO SOMEONE. Learn it from the situation, not from a translation rule.

1) CITIES: J’habite à Montréal. Je travaille à Paris. Je vais à Toronto. Usually use À before a city name.
2) COUNTRIES: J’habite au Canada, en France, aux États-Unis. Country names use AU / EN / AUX depending on gender and number. EN is a different form: do not say “à France”. For today, remember these three examples.
3) PLACES: Je vais au supermarché. Je suis à la maison. Je vais à l’école. Je vais aux toilettes.
4) PEOPLE: Je parle à Marie. Je parle au professeur. Je donne le cahier à mon ami.
5) CLOCK TIME: Je travaille à huit heures.

À WITH AN ARTICLE — ONE SIMPLE TABLE
à + le = AU : au supermarché / au professeur
à + la = À LA : à la maison
à + l’ = À L’ : à l’école
à + les = AUX : aux toilettes
Never write “à le” or “à les”. With a city or name: à Montréal / à Marie.
Check the accent: Il A un livre (avoir); il va À l’école (preposition).

STOP — SAY THESE FOUR SENTENCES BEFORE CONTINUING
I live in Montréal. → J’habite à Montréal.
I go to the supermarket. → Je vais au supermarché.
I speak to the teacher. → Je parle au professeur.
I work at eight. → Je travaille à huit heures.

PART B — DE FAMILY (AFTER À IS CLEAR)
Start with ONE idea: DE often connects FROM, OF / BELONGING or ABOUT.
1) ORIGIN: Je suis de Montréal. (Later: Je viens de Montréal.)
2) BELONGING: Le livre de Marie. Le cahier du professeur. La porte de la chambre.
3) TALKING ABOUT: Je parle de mon travail. Je parle du professeur.

DE WITH AN ARTICLE — ONE SIMPLE TABLE
 de + le = DU : du professeur
 de + la = DE LA : de la chambre
 de + l’ = DE L’ : de l’appartement
 de + les = DES : des étudiants
Never write “de le” or “de les”. With a name: de Marie. With mon/ma/mes: de mon ami, not du mon ami.

STOP — CHECK THE MEANING
Je parle AU professeur = I speak TO the teacher.
Je parle DU professeur = I speak ABOUT the teacher.
Je vais AU supermarché = I go TO the supermarket.
(We will add “Je viens DU supermarché” when we learn venir on Day 33.)

PART C — FOOD (SIMILAR WORDS, DIFFERENT MEANING)
For an unspecified amount of food, use DU / DE LA / DE L’ / DES.
Je mange DU pain. Je mange DE LA salade. Je prends DE L’eau. Je mange DES pommes.
Compare the meanings: J’aime LE fromage = I like cheese in general; Je mange DU fromage = I eat some cheese.
DU in “le cahier DU professeur” means DE + LE. DU in “du pain” means an unspecified quantity. Same spelling, different job.
DES in “je parle DES étudiants” means ABOUT THE students (de + les). DES in “je cherche DES étudiants” means SOME students.
With basic negation of an unspecified quantity: Je mange du pain → Je ne mange pas DE pain; Je mange des pommes → Je ne mange pas DE pommes.
But likes keep LE / LA / LES: Je n’aime pas LE fromage.

THREE SIMPLE DECISIONS
1) TO / AT / TO WHOM? Think À family. FROM / OF / ABOUT? Think DE family.
2) If LE, LA, L’ or LES comes next, use the family table.
3) FOOD amount? Think DU / DE LA / DE L’ / DES; general liking? Think LE / LA / L’ / LES.
These are beginner shortcuts, not rules for every French sentence. No extra country exceptions or advanced cases today.

MON HISTOIRE DU JOUR — READ / COPY / SAY
J’habite à Montréal dans un petit appartement. Le matin, je vais à l’école et je parle au professeur. Mon cahier est dans mon sac. Je parle de mon travail avec mon ami. À midi, je mange du pain et de la pizza. Le soir, je suis à la maison.
Copy the story once, understand it, and read it aloud twice. No extra comprehension questions.

PRACTISE FOR USE, NOT JUST MARKS
First complete the À-only examples, then the DE-only examples, then food and mixed meaning. Say each answer before writing it.
At the end, give three TRUE sentences: a place you go, a person you talk about, and something you eat. Models are examples, not required personal answers.
If time is short, prioritize these three true sentences and correcting wrong answers over repeating already-correct drills.

days.explanation:
DAY 30 — SIMPLE STUDENT NOTES
GOAL: Conjugate regular attendre; distinguish knowing a person/place (connaître) from knowing a fact/how (savoir), and use both naturally.
ESTIMATED TIME: 50–60 minutes; 3 verbs, only 3 new nouns

0. ACTIVE RECALL BEFORE LEARNING (6–8 MIN)
Scheduled spaced review: Day 16, Day 23, Day 27, Day 29. The first attempt is WITHOUT notes.
Say or write ONE anchor from every due day, plus articles for 2–3 older nouns. Record any error and retry it tomorrow.
Five flashcards below review older material only; current lesson items appear in the practice below.

MEANING FIRST
attendre = to wait for. J’attends mon ami. In French, attendre takes its object directly: NOT “j’attends pour mon ami.”
connaître = to know / be familiar with A PERSON, A PLACE or A THING. Je connais ce professeur. Je connais Montréal.
savoir = to know a FACT / ANSWER, or HOW TO do something. Je sais la réponse. Je sais lire en français.
Simple starter: KNOW a person/place → usually connaître. KNOW HOW to do something → savoir + infinitive. For an answer or fact, both “Je sais la réponse” and “Je connais la réponse” can be correct. Do not treat this as a strict one-word-only rule.

THE PATTERNS
attendre is regular -RE: j’attends, tu attends, il attend, nous attendons, vous attendez, ils attendent.
connaître: je connais, tu connais, il connaît, nous connaissons, vous connaissez, ils connaissent. Watch il connaît (î) and nous connaissons (ss).
savoir: je sais, tu sais, il sait, nous savons, vous savez, ils savent.
Say three useful chunks aloud: J’attends mon ami. Je connais le professeur. Je sais la réponse.

USE DAY 29, NOT EXTRA THEORY
J’attends à l’école. Je parle de mon rendez-vous. Je connais le professeur de cette école.
Ask someone a real question: Tu connais cette personne ? / Tu sais la réponse ?
After checking, say one true sentence about a place you know and one fact you know.

MON HISTOIRE DU JOUR — READ / COPY / SAY
Aujourd’hui, j’attends mon ami à l’école. Je connais mon professeur et je connais bien cette école. Mon ami arrive avec son cahier, mais il ne connaît pas la réponse. Je sais la réponse et j’explique la question. Ensuite, nous étudions le français ensemble dans la petite classe.
Copy the story once, understand it, and read it aloud twice. There are no separate story comprehension questions.

HOW TO PRACTISE (DON’T JUST COMPLETE EXERCISES)
1) Recall → 2) say the sentence aloud → 3) write/type → 4) check → 5) repair the error and retry tomorrow.
Translate 4–6 practical sentences and answer personal spoken questions WITHOUT reading the model first.
For personal writing and speaking, the answer is only a MODEL. Choose what is true for you, add a detail, and accept other correct answers.
End by using today’s target in a NEW sentence or 20–30 seconds of speech. Mark independent / needed hint / read model.

days.explanation:
DAY 31 — SIMPLE STUDENT NOTES
GOAL: Communicate ability, wishes and obligations using three common irregular verbs + an infinitive, then create genuine personal responses.
ESTIMATED TIME: 50–60 minutes; reduced vocabulary

0. ACTIVE RECALL BEFORE LEARNING (6–8 MIN)
Scheduled spaced review: Day 1, Day 17, Day 24, Day 28, Day 30. The first attempt is WITHOUT notes.
Say or write ONE anchor from every due day, plus articles for 2–3 older nouns. Record any error and retry it tomorrow.
Five flashcards below review older material only; current lesson items appear in the practice below.

THREE IDEAS, ONE USEFUL SENTENCE SHAPE
Je PEUX = I can. Je VEUX = I want. Je DOIS = I have to. These are different meanings, not interchangeable.
Shape: PERSON + pouvoir/vouloir/devoir (conjugated) + OTHER VERB in the INFINITIVE.
Je peux parler français. Je veux apprendre le français. Je dois travailler.
Only the FIRST verb changes: Nous pouvons parler (not “nous pouvons parlons”).
After this pattern, the second verb stays in its dictionary form: lire, finir, aller, apprendre.

CONJUGATION - READ AND COMPARE
pouvoir: je peux, tu peux, il peut, nous pouvons, vous pouvez, ils peuvent.
vouloir: je veux, tu veux, il veut, nous voulons, vous voulez, ils veulent.
devoir: je dois, tu dois, il doit, nous devons, vous devez, ils doivent.
Listen for different forms in conversation; memorize je / nous / ils before trying fast responses.

REAL-LIFE USE
ABILITY: Je peux lire cette phrase. / Je ne peux pas travailler. Today, use infinitives already learned: parler, lire or aller.
WISH: Je veux apprendre le français. Polite request forms come later; today practise only je veux + an infinitive.
OBLIGATION: Je dois finir mes devoirs. / Tu dois attendre. This is “must/have to”, not a future tense.
ASK: Tu peux aider ton ami ? / Tu veux étudier ? / Tu dois travailler aujourd’hui ?
Say one TRUE sentence beginning with Je peux…, Je veux…, Je dois….

COMMON ERRORS
Incorrect: Je veux parle français. Correct: Je veux PARLER français.
Incorrect: Nous devons travaillons. Correct: Nous devons TRAVAILLER.
Incorrect: Je peux à lire. Correct: Je peux LIRE. No à or de between these modal verbs and the infinitive in these simple patterns.

MON HISTOIRE DU JOUR — READ / COPY / SAY
Le matin, je veux étudier le français. Je peux travailler avec mon ami, mais nous devons finir notre devoir. Il veut lire un livre et je veux écrire une phrase. Ensuite, nous pouvons parler français. Mon ami ne peut pas travailler longtemps, mais il veut apprendre demain.
Copy the story once, understand it, and read it aloud twice. There are no separate story comprehension questions.

HOW TO PRACTISE (DON’T JUST COMPLETE EXERCISES)
1) Recall → 2) say the sentence aloud → 3) write/type → 4) check → 5) repair the error and retry tomorrow.
Translate 4–6 practical sentences and answer personal spoken questions WITHOUT reading the model first.
For personal writing and speaking, the supplied answer is ONLY an example; other accurate answers are valid.
End by using today’s target in a NEW sentence or 20–30 seconds of speech. Mark independent / needed hint / read model.
fixed: Je peux parler français. — I can speak French.
Je veux apprendre le français. — I want to learn French.
Je dois finir mon travail. — I must finish my work.

days.explanation:
DAY 32 — SIMPLE STUDENT NOTES
GOAL: Learn independent present-tense patterns for voir and boire; use food quantity articles from Day 29 and distinguish voir (see) from regarder (watch/look at).
ESTIMATED TIME: 45–50 minutes

0. ACTIVE RECALL BEFORE LEARNING (6–8 MIN)
Scheduled spaced review: Day 2, Day 18, Day 25, Day 29, Day 31. The first attempt is WITHOUT notes.
Say or write ONE anchor from every due day, plus articles for 2–3 older nouns. Record any error and retry it tomorrow.
Five flashcards below review older material only; current lesson items appear in the practice below.

TWO DIFFERENT VERBS
voir = to see (something enters your sight). Je vois mon ami. Je vois l’école.
regarder = to look at / watch (you direct your attention). Je regarde la télévision. Je regarde ce livre.
boire = to drink. Je bois de l’eau. Nous buvons du jus.
Voir and boire have DIFFERENT present conjugations. Learn them separately, even though je vois / je bois sound similar.

PRESENT FORMS
voir: je vois, tu vois, il voit, nous voyons, vous voyez, ils voient.
boire: je bois, tu bois, il boit, nous buvons, vous buvez, ils boivent.
Pronunciation observation: je vois and je bois rhyme; spellings and nous / ils forms differ.

CONNECT WITH DAY 29
Je bois DU jus. Je bois DE L’eau. Je prends UNE tasse.
Je ne bois pas DE jus. After a negated unspecified amount, use de/d’.
Say two real sentences: what you drink, and what you can see around you.

MON HISTOIRE DU JOUR — READ / COPY / SAY
Aujourd’hui, je vais au café avec ma sœur. Je bois de l’eau et elle boit du jus. Nous regardons les petites tables et nous voyons notre professeur dans le café. Je prends mon cahier et je lis une phrase. Ma sœur regarde le menu et choisit une boisson.
Copy the story once, understand it, and read it aloud twice. There are no separate story comprehension questions.

HOW TO PRACTISE (DON’T JUST COMPLETE EXERCISES)
1) Recall → 2) say the sentence aloud → 3) write/type → 4) check → 5) repair the error and retry tomorrow.
Translate 4–6 practical sentences and answer personal spoken questions WITHOUT reading the model first.
For personal writing and speaking, the supplied answer is ONLY an example; other accurate answers are valid.
End by using today’s target in a NEW sentence or 20–30 seconds of speech. Mark independent / needed hint / read model.

Je regarde le professeur. — I look at the teacher.

days.title: Venir et recevoir — venir de, recevoir un message
days.focus: Practise two different irregular present patterns, use venir de + PLACE for origin, and communicate about receiving something.
days.yesterday: Due now: Day 3, Day 19, Day 26, Day 30, Day 32. Also retry yesterday’s personal errors. Start WITHOUT the answer key; review +1/+3/+7/+14/+30.
days.explanation:
DAY 33 — SIMPLE STUDENT NOTES
GOAL: Practise two different irregular present patterns, use venir de + PLACE for origin, and communicate about receiving something.
ESTIMATED TIME: 45–50 minutes

0. ACTIVE RECALL BEFORE LEARNING (6–8 MIN)
Scheduled spaced review: Day 3, Day 19, Day 26, Day 30, Day 32. The first attempt is WITHOUT notes.
Say or write ONE anchor from every due day, plus articles for 2–3 older nouns. Record any error and retry it tomorrow.
Five flashcards below review older material only; current lesson items appear in the practice below.

MEANING AND USE
venir = to come. Mon ami vient à la maison. Nous venons à l’école.
venir DE + a PLACE = to come FROM. Je viens de Montréal. Je viens du supermarché. Je viens de l’école.
recevoir = to receive. Je reçois un message. Nous recevons une lettre. These are two different conjugation families.
Today, use venir de + PLACE for origin only. Another meaning of venir de will be taught later.

TWO PRESENT PATTERNS
venir: je viens, tu viens, il vient, nous venons, vous venez, ils viennent.
recevoir: je reçois, tu reçois, il reçoit, nous recevons, vous recevez, ils reçoivent.
The c in je reçois has cedilla (ç), but nous recevons has ordinary c. Say je reçois / nous recevons / ils reçoivent aloud.

USE À AND DE NATURALLY
Je viens DU supermarché = I come FROM the supermarket. / Je vais AU supermarché = I go TO the supermarket.
Il vient DE l’école. / Il va À l’école.
Je reçois un message DU professeur (from the teacher). Other meanings of de depend on context.
Say where you come from and one thing you receive; these should be personal answers, not copied from the model.

MON HISTOIRE DU JOUR — READ / COPY / SAY
Ce matin, mon ami vient à la maison. Il vient de Montréal et il connaît bien ma sœur. Je reçois un message de mon professeur et je réponds rapidement. Ensuite, nous recevons un petit colis. Mon ami ouvre le colis et voit un livre. Nous lisons ensemble dans le salon.
Copy the story once, understand it, and read it aloud twice. There are no separate story comprehension questions.

days.explanation:
DAY 34 — SIMPLE STUDENT NOTES
GOAL: Understand faire as an everyday action/expression verb; practise priority uses in sports, weather, household tasks, studies and shopping without overloading.
ESTIMATED TIME: 50–60 minutes (one new verb, rich uses)

0. ACTIVE RECALL BEFORE LEARNING (6–8 MIN)
Scheduled spaced review: Day 4, Day 20, Day 27, Day 31, Day 33. The first attempt is WITHOUT notes.
Say or write ONE anchor from every due day, plus articles for 2–3 older nouns. Record any error and retry it tomorrow.
Five flashcards below review older material only; current lesson items appear in the practice below.

FAIRE = MUCH MORE THAN TO DO OR MAKE
In French, FAIRE is used in many fixed everyday expressions. Translate the WHOLE CHUNK, not each word. MUST MASTER TODAY: faire du sport, du vélo, de la natation; il fait chaud/froid/beau; faire la cuisine, le ménage, la vaisselle, les devoirs, les courses. RECOGNIZE ONLY: other expressions below.
Conjugation: je fais, tu fais, il/elle fait, nous faisons, vous faites, ils/elles font.
Pronunciation: nous faisons ≈ “nou feuzon” [nu fə.zɔ̃]. Vous faites is NOT “vous faisez”; ils font is NOT “ils faisent”.

CORE USE 1 — SPORTS AND ACTIVITIES
Je fais DU sport. = I exercise / play sports.
Je fais DU vélo. = I cycle / go biking.
Elle fait DE LA natation. = She goes swimming.
Heard less often in this beginner lesson: faire DE L’escalade. Learn the pattern, but do not memorize a new sport list.
For many team sports you may hear “jouer au football” (to play football). Recognize this expression only; we are not teaching a second new verb today.
Notice du / de la / de l’ are chunks with sports; use the article that belongs to the noun.

CORE USE 2 — WEATHER (IMPERSONAL IL)
Il fait chaud. = It is hot. / Il fait froid. = It is cold. / Il fait beau. = The weather is nice.
Il fait mauvais temps. = The weather is bad. / Il fait 20 degrés. = It is 20 degrees.
Weather uses IL fait. Personal feeling uses J’AI chaud / J’AI froid (avoir), not “je fais chaud”.
Not all weather uses faire: “Il pleut” = it is raining, but this extra weather verb is recognition only.

CORE USE 3 — HOME, SCHOOL, SHOPPING
Je fais LA cuisine. = I cook.
Je fais LE ménage. = I clean the house.
Je fais LA vaisselle. = I wash the dishes.
Je fais MES devoirs. = I do my homework.
Nous faisons LES courses. = We do the shopping / grocery shopping.
Je fais UNE pause. = I take a break. Notice these expressions require different articles: do not say “je fais du courses”.

RECOGNIZE ONLY — USEFUL EXPRESSIONS FOR LATER
Je fais attention (à...). = I pay attention (to...).
Je fais la queue. = I wait in line.
Ça fait quinze dollars. = That comes to $15.
Ça fait du bien. = That feels good.
Je fais une promenade. = I take a walk.
Je fais confiance à mon ami. = I trust my friend.
Do not memorize all of these today. Recognize their meaning; practise and recycle them in future weeks.

FOCUS ON PERSONAL SPEAKING, NOT COPYING
Quick switch: Je fais du sport → Nous faisons du sport → Elle fait du sport.
Answer from real life: Tu fais du sport ? Quel temps fait-il aujourd’hui ? Qui fait la cuisine chez toi ?
Tell a 20–30 second story with at least THREE different uses: sport + weather + home/shopping.
Do not teach the advanced causative faire + infinitive (“faire réparer”) yet.

MON HISTOIRE DU JOUR — READ / COPY / SAY
Le samedi, je fais du sport avec mon ami. Il fait beau, mais il fait un peu froid. Ensuite, nous faisons les courses au supermarché. À la maison, je fais la cuisine et mon ami fait la vaisselle. Le soir, nous faisons une pause et nous parlons français.
Copy the story once, understand it, and read it aloud twice. There are no separate story comprehension questions.

0. ACTIVE RECALL BEFORE LEARNING (6–8 MIN)
Scheduled spaced review: Day 5, Day 21, Day 28, Day 32, Day 34. The first attempt is WITHOUT notes.
Say or write ONE anchor from every due day, plus articles for 2–3 older nouns. Record any error and retry it tomorrow.
Five flashcards below review older material only; current lesson items appear in the practice below.

TODAY IS A REAL CHECK-UP
NO NEW VERBS, NO NEW GRAMMAR, NO NEW VOCABULARY. First try everything WITHOUT the table or the teacher model.
Warm-up (5–8 min): from memory write je/nous/ils for pouvoir, vouloir, devoir, venir, recevoir, faire. Say 2 -ER, 2 -IR and 2 Week-4 -RE forms too.
Grammar check: tell the difference between je parle AU professeur and je parle DU professeur; j’aime LE pain and je mange DU pain.
Accuracy check: je veux parler (NOT je veux parle); nous faisons (NOT faions); je ne mange pas de pain.
Real-life communication goal: answer 5 new questions with complete sentences and NO reading.

SPEAKING ASSESSMENT — 60–90 SECONDS
Prompt: Introduce your city, say what you CAN / WANT / MUST do, describe what you drink/eat, describe the weather, and talk about a person or place you know.
Use at least six different verbs; include faire in two DIFFERENT senses (e.g., weather + activity). Use one à expression and one de expression.
The oral model is ONLY a possible answer: accept all accurate personal answers. Do not penalize originality.
Teacher records: independent / needed prompting / read the model; note TWO errors to repair tomorrow.

SHORT WRITING & NEXT-DAY REPAIR
Write 6–8 sentences about an ordinary day. Include an À destination, a DE connection, a food quantity, a modal + infinitive and one faire chunk.
Check gender/articles, verb endings, negation and accents after writing (not while drafting).
If a verb family causes repeated errors, revisit that family tomorrow BEFORE adding more. Measure progress by independent answers, not by the number of completed exercises. Teacher checks: accuracy, intelligibility, and need for prompts.

MON HISTOIRE DU JOUR — READ / COPY / SAY
Le matin, je fais mes devoirs et je prends mon sac. Je peux aller au parc, mais je dois finir mon travail. Mon ami vient à la maison et nous buvons de l’eau. Il connaît mon professeur et il comprend la leçon. Ensuite, nous faisons du vélo et nous parlons de notre journée.

Je connais bien mon professeur et je comprends les questions simples. Je peux lire et écrire en français, mais je veux apprendre de nouveaux mots. Aujourd’hui, je dois finir mes devoirs. Il fait beau, alors je peux aller au parc. Le samedi, je fais du vélo avec mon ami et nous faisons les courses au supermarché. Le soir, nous faisons la cuisine et nous parlons de notre journée. J’aime apprendre le français !
